title: Employee Onboarding Guide
summary: Complete guide for welcoming new employees
content: This comprehensive guide covers all steps for onboarding new employees including paperwork, system access provisioning, team introductions, and the first-week schedule. HR coordinators should use this document to ensure a smooth transition for all new hires. The checklist includes background check completion, equipment setup, badge issuance, and benefits enrollment.

title: Annual Leave Policy
summary: Explains annual leave entitlements and procedures
content: Employees are entitled to 20 days of annual leave per year, accrued monthly. Leave requests must be submitted at least 5 working days in advance via the HR portal. Unused leave may be carried forward up to 10 days into the following calendar year. Leave encashment is available upon resignation after 1 year of service.

title: Work From Home Policy
summary: Guidelines for remote work arrangements
content: Employees may work from home up to 3 days per week with manager approval. A stable internet connection and a suitable workspace are mandatory requirements. Security policies including VPN usage must be followed at all times. Remote employees must be available during core hours (10 AM – 4 PM local time).

title: Code of Conduct
summary: Company standards for professional behavior
content: All employees are expected to maintain a respectful, inclusive, and professional workplace. Harassment, discrimination, and unethical behavior will result in disciplinary action up to and including termination. Report violations confidentially to HR or through the anonymous ethics hotline.

title: Performance Review Process
summary: How to conduct and prepare for performance reviews
content: Performance reviews are conducted bi-annually in June and December. Employees must complete a self-assessment form at least two weeks before their review meeting. Managers score employees on five competency areas: Communication, Collaboration, Innovation, Execution, and Growth. Outcomes determine bonus eligibility and promotion consideration.

title: Grievance Handling Procedure
summary: Step-by-step process for raising and resolving grievances
content: Employees who have a workplace grievance should first attempt informal resolution with their immediate manager. If unresolved within 5 days, a formal grievance form must be submitted to HR. HR will investigate and respond within 15 working days. Appeals can be escalated to the HR Director.

title: Employee Benefits Overview
summary: Summary of all employee benefits
content: Benefits include: health insurance (employee + family), dental and vision coverage, life insurance of 3× annual salary, a 401(k) plan with 5% employer match, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP). Enrollment is during the first 30 days of employment or at the annual open enrollment period each November.

title: Disciplinary Action Policy
summary: Process for addressing employee misconduct
content: Disciplinary actions follow a progressive sequence: verbal warning, written warning, final written warning, and termination. Serious misconduct such as theft or harassment may result in immediate termination. All actions are documented and retained in the employee's personnel file for five years.

title: Diversity and Inclusion Policy
summary: Company commitment to a diverse and inclusive workplace
content: We are committed to building a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. Hiring decisions are based solely on merit. We host quarterly DEI training sessions and maintain an Employee Resource Group (ERG) program. Discrimination or exclusion of any kind is strictly prohibited and reportable.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement
summary: Policy for business travel and expense claims
content: Business travel must be pre-approved by the department head. Economy class is standard for flights under 4 hours. Hotel accommodation should not exceed $200/night. Expense claims with receipts must be submitted within 30 days of travel. Use the Concur expense management system.

title: VPN Setup Guide
summary: How to install and configure the company VPN
content: Download the Cisco AnyConnect client from the IT portal. Enter server address vpn.company.com. Use your Active Directory credentials to authenticate. MFA is required — approve the Duo push notification on your registered device. Contact the helpdesk if you encounter certificate errors.

title: Password Reset Procedure
summary: Steps to reset your network or application password
content: Visit password.company.com and click 'Reset Password'. Verify your identity via email OTP or manager approval. New passwords must be at least 12 characters and include uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Passwords expire every 90 days. Do not reuse the last 10 passwords.

title: Software Request Process
summary: How to request new software installation
content: Submit a software request through the ServiceNow portal under 'IT Requests'. Include the business justification and software name/version. Requests are reviewed within 3 business days. Only approved and licensed software may be installed. Contact the help desk for urgent requests.

title: Printer Setup — Floor 3
summary: Configure the network printer on the third floor
content: Go to Settings > Printers > Add a printer. Select 'HP LaserJet-Floor3' from the network list. Driver installation is automatic. Default print settings are duplex and grayscale. For color printing, select 'HP Color — Floor3' and note it is charged to your department cost code.

title: Email Configuration in Outlook
summary: Set up company email in Outlook
content: Open Outlook and add a new account. Enter your company email address. Outlook will auto-configure settings via Autodiscover. Enter your Active Directory password when prompted. Enable MFA if not already configured. Sync frequency should be set to 'As items arrive' for best performance.

title: Laptop Refresh Program
summary: Guidelines for the biennial laptop refresh initiative
content: Laptops are replaced on a 3-year cycle. Eligible employees receive an email with instructions to schedule a replacement appointment. Before the replacement, back up all data to OneDrive or the shared drive. Submit your old laptop to IT within 5 days of receiving the new one. Data wiping is performed to DoD standards.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication Setup
summary: How to enroll and use MFA for company systems
content: MFA is mandatory for all employees. Download the Duo Mobile app on your smartphone. Visit mfa.company.com and click 'Enroll'. Scan the QR code in the Duo app. Test authentication by logging into the company portal. If you lose your device, call the helpdesk immediately to deactivate the old device.

title: ServiceNow Ticketing Guide
summary: How to create and manage IT support tickets
content: Log in to servicenow.company.com with your company credentials. Click 'Submit a Request' for new issues or 'View My Tickets' to track existing ones. Assign priority as: Critical (system down), High (major impact), Medium (partial impact), Low (minor issue). Expected resolution times are SLA-defined: Critical 4h, High 8h, Medium 24h, Low 72h.

title: Data Backup and Recovery
summary: Company data backup policy and recovery procedures
content: All company data must reside on approved storage (SharePoint, OneDrive, network drives). Local-only data is not backed up. Backup frequency: daily incremental, weekly full. Recovery requests are submitted via ServiceNow and fulfilled within 4 hours for critical data and 24 hours for standard data.

title: Cybersecurity Awareness Training
summary: Annual cybersecurity training requirements
content: All employees must complete the annual cybersecurity awareness training by Q1. Topics include phishing recognition, password hygiene, social engineering, and data classification. Training is available on the LMS (learning.company.com). Completion is mandatory and tracked; non-compliance may result in disciplinary action.

title: Data Center Overview
summary: Overview of company data center locations and policies
content: The company operates two data centers: Primary (Chicago) and DR (Dallas). Access is restricted to authorized Infrastructure team members. Visitors must be escorted at all times. All changes to production infrastructure must follow the change management process and be approved by the Infrastructure Manager.

title: Network Diagram Documentation
summary: Current network topology and IP addressing scheme
content: The corporate network uses a 10.0.0.0/8 address space. VLAN segmentation is used for departments: IT (VLAN 10), HR (VLAN 20), Finance (VLAN 30), Operations (VLAN 40). The perimeter is protected by Palo Alto firewalls with IDS/IPS enabled. Network diagrams are stored in the Infrastructure SharePoint.

title: Server Patching Schedule
summary: Monthly server patching window and procedures
content: Server patching occurs on the second Tuesday of each month (Patch Tuesday) between 11 PM and 3 AM. All patches are tested in the UAT environment first. A change ticket must be raised 5 days in advance. The Infrastructure team sends notifications to affected stakeholders 24 hours before maintenance.

title: Cloud Infrastructure — AWS Overview
summary: Overview of our AWS cloud environment
content: Production workloads run in us-east-1 and us-west-2 for failover. AWS Organizations is used for account governance. All resources are tagged with cost_center, environment, and owner. Cost alerts are configured at $10K monthly spend per account. IAM roles follow least-privilege principles.

title: Disaster Recovery Plan
summary: Business continuity and disaster recovery procedures
content: RTO is 4 hours and RPO is 1 hour for Tier-1 systems. The DR failover test is conducted bi-annually. In the event of a declared disaster, the Infrastructure Manager initiates the DR runbook. Critical services are redirected to the Dallas DR site via DNS failover. Communication is via the company emergency notification system.

title: Firewall Rules Management
summary: How to request and manage firewall rule changes
content: Firewall change requests are submitted via ServiceNow. Requestors must provide source IP/range, destination IP/range, port/protocol, and business justification. Changes are reviewed by the Security team and approved by the CISO. Production firewall changes require a CAB approval. Changes are implemented during the maintenance window.

title: DNS and DHCP Management
summary: Managing DNS records and DHCP leases
content: DNS is managed via Microsoft DNS servers. New DNS records are created by submitting a request to the Infrastructure team. DHCP leases are dynamically assigned with a 8-hour lease time. Static reservations are used for servers and printers. The DHCP scope is documented in the IPAM system.

title: SSL Certificate Management
summary: Procedure for managing SSL/TLS certificates
content: All external-facing services must use certificates from the approved CA (DigiCert). Internal services use the company's internal CA. Certificate expiry monitoring is automated via Datadog. Renewals must be initiated 30 days before expiry. The PKI team manages all certificate issuance and revocation.

title: Load Balancer Configuration
summary: F5 BIG-IP load balancer configuration guide
content: Load balancer changes are requested via ServiceNow. The Infrastructure team configures F5 virtual servers, pools, and health monitors. Health check intervals are set to 5 seconds with 3 retries. Session persistence is cookie-based for web applications. Changes to production require CAB approval.

title: Storage Array Management
summary: Managing the NetApp SAN environment
content: Storage provisioning requests are handled by the Infrastructure team. New LUNs are created from the appropriate storage tier (Tier 1: SSD, Tier 2: SAS). Capacity alerts fire at 80% utilization. Snapshots are taken hourly and retained for 7 days. Annual storage reviews are conducted to reclaim unused space.

title: New Employee IT Checklist
summary: IT setup checklist for new employees
content: Complete these tasks on your first day: 1) Collect your laptop from IT reception. 2) Log in with your temporary credentials and change your password. 3) Set up MFA. 4) Configure VPN. 5) Set up Outlook email. 6) Install required software via the Software Center. 7) Join your team's Microsoft Teams channel. Contact the helpdesk if you need assistance.

title: How to Use Microsoft Teams
summary: Guide for using Microsoft Teams for collaboration
content: Teams is our primary collaboration platform. Create channels within your team for specific projects. Use @mentions to notify specific people. Video calls: Click the camera icon to start a meeting. Screen sharing: Click the share icon during a call. Files shared in Teams are stored in the corresponding SharePoint folder. Integrate your calendar to see meeting invites.

title: SharePoint File Management
summary: How to store and share files using SharePoint
content: Store all project files in the appropriate SharePoint site for your team. Use versioning to track changes — do not save multiple copies with different names. Sharing with external parties requires manager approval and must use guest access only (not public links). Unused files should be archived after 2 years.

title: Company Communication Guidelines
summary: Best practices for internal and external communication
content: Emails should be concise and professional. Use Clear Subject Lines. CC only those who need to be aware. BCC should not be used internally. For urgent issues use Teams or phone. Customer-facing emails must be proofread and use the approved signature template. Avoid using personal email for company business.

title: Project Management Basics
summary: Introduction to project management at the company
content: The company uses Agile methodology with 2-week sprint cycles. All projects must be registered in the PMO system. Use the project charter template for new initiatives. Weekly status reports are required for active projects. Project managers must have PMP certification or be enrolled in the certification program.

title: Excel Training for Beginners
summary: Basic Excel skills every employee should know
content: Cover the basics: data entry, formatting, SUM/AVERAGE/COUNT formulas, sorting and filtering, and creating simple charts. Use the provided training workbook on the LMS. Practice exercises are included. Intermediate topics: VLOOKUP, pivot tables, and conditional formatting are covered in the follow-up course.

title: PowerPoint Presentation Standards
summary: Company standards for business presentations
content: Use the approved PowerPoint template (available in the Brand Portal). Maximum 10 slides for a 30-minute meeting. Use sans-serif fonts (Calibri or Segoe UI) at minimum 18pt for body text. Avoid cluttered slides — one idea per slide. Include slide numbers and a consistent footer with the company logo.

title: Data Privacy Training
summary: Training on data privacy laws and company obligations
content: All employees who handle personal data must complete this annual training. Topics: GDPR principles, data subject rights, lawful basis for processing, data breach reporting (72-hour rule), and how to handle subject access requests. Training is on the LMS. Completion deadline is March 31 each year.

title: Health and Safety Induction
summary: Workplace health and safety orientation for new starters
content: All new employees must complete the health and safety induction before their second day. Topics covered: fire evacuation procedures, first aid kit locations, ergonomic workstation setup, and incident reporting. The induction is conducted in person by the Facilities team and online via the LMS.

title: Leadership Development Program
summary: Overview of the leadership development program
content: The 6-month leadership development program is open to employees at Grade 7+ with manager nomination. The program includes monthly workshops, a personal mentor, a cross-functional project, and a final presentation to the Executive team. Applications open in February each year. Contact HR for the nomination form.

title: Monthly Expense Report Submission
summary: How to submit your monthly expense report
content: Expense reports must be submitted by the 5th of the following month. Log into Concur at expenses.company.com. Add each expense with a receipt, cost code, and business justification. Reports are approved by your line manager and then processed by Finance. Payments are made with the monthly payroll run.

title: Purchase Order Process
summary: How to raise and approve purchase orders
content: All purchases over $500 require a purchase order (PO). Log into the ERP system and create a new PO. Include vendor name, item description, quantity, unit price, and GL code. Approvals are tiered: $500–$5000 (Manager), $5000–$50000 (Director), $50000+ (CFO). Goods receipt must be confirmed in the ERP before the invoice is paid.

title: Budget Planning Process
summary: Annual budget planning guidelines
content: Budget planning begins in October for the following fiscal year. Department heads submit budget requests by October 31. Finance consolidates requests and presents scenarios to the Executive team in November. Final budgets are approved by the Board in December and communicated to departments in January.

title: Invoice Approval Workflow
summary: Process for approving and paying vendor invoices
content: Vendor invoices are received by the Finance inbox (invoices@company.com). Invoices are matched against the PO in the ERP. If matched, they are auto-approved. Exceptions are routed to the budget owner for approval. Payment terms are Net-30 by default. Early payment discounts are taken if the discount rate exceeds the company's cost of capital.

title: Chart of Accounts Reference
summary: Reference guide for GL codes and cost centers
content: The chart of accounts is organized by: 1000s (Assets), 2000s (Liabilities), 3000s (Equity), 4000s (Revenue), 5000s (Cost of Sales), 6000s (Operating Expenses). Always use the correct GL code when raising POs and expense reports. New GL codes can only be created by the Finance Controller with CFO approval.

title: Payroll Processing Schedule
summary: Payroll cutoff dates and processing timeline
content: Payroll is processed monthly. Cutoff for timesheet submission is the 25th of each month. Any changes (starters, leavers, salary changes) must be submitted to HR by the 20th. Payslips are available in the employee self-service portal on the last working day of the month. Direct deposit is the only payment method.

title: Accounts Payable Procedures
summary: Standard accounts payable procedures
content: AP processes all vendor invoices within 5 business days of receipt. Duplicate invoice detection is automated. Payment runs are on Wednesdays for electronic payments. Vendor banking details can only be changed after a verification call to the vendor at the number on file. Maintain audit trail for all changes.

title: Financial Reporting Calendar
summary: Key dates for financial reporting and close
content: Month-end close: 5 business days after month end. Quarter-end close: 10 business days after quarter end. Year-end close: 20 business days after December 31. Flash P&L is shared with leadership on day 3 of close. Finance team members must not take leave during close periods without prior CFO approval.

title: Cost Centre Management
summary: How cost centres are created and managed
content: Cost centres are aligned to organizational units. A new cost centre is requested by the department head with CFO approval. Cost centre owners are responsible for monitoring spend versus budget. Monthly variance reports are distributed on day 7 of the new month. Reforecasting is allowed twice per fiscal year.

title: Audit Preparation Guide
summary: How to prepare for internal and external audits
content: Auditors require access to invoices, POs, expense reports, and approval trails for the audit period. All requested documents must be provided within 24 hours. Do not alter or delete documents under audit review. Coordinate document preparation through the Finance Controller. Debrief sessions are held after each audit.

title: Incident Management Procedure
summary: How to report and manage operational incidents
content: An incident is any unplanned interruption to a service. All incidents must be logged in ServiceNow within 15 minutes of discovery. Severity levels: P1 (business-critical), P2 (major impact), P3 (minor impact). P1 incidents trigger a war room and executive notification. Incident commanders are designated on a rotation schedule.

title: Change Management Process
summary: How to raise and approve change requests
content: All changes to production systems must be raised in ServiceNow as a Change Request. Change types: Standard (pre-approved), Normal (CAB review required), Emergency (post-implementation review). The CAB meets every Tuesday. Change freeze periods apply during Q4 and major business events.

title: Problem Management Process
summary: Root cause analysis and problem management
content: Problems are raised from repeat incidents or P1 incidents. A Problem Manager is assigned and conducts root cause analysis within 5 business days. Workarounds are documented in the knowledge base while permanent fixes are implemented. Problem records are closed only after the root cause is confirmed resolved.

title: Standard Operating Procedures Overview
summary: How to write and maintain standard operating procedures
content: SOPs must use the approved template (available in the Operations SharePoint). Include: purpose, scope, owner, review frequency (annual), and step-by-step instructions. All SOPs must be reviewed by the department head and approved by the Operations Manager. Outdated SOPs are archived, not deleted.

title: Business Continuity Planning
summary: Business continuity planning requirements
content: Each department must maintain a BCP that is tested annually. The BCP includes: critical function identification, recovery time objectives, alternate work locations, and key contact lists. BCPs are stored in the Risk Management SharePoint. The annual BCP test is coordinated by the Risk Manager in Q3.

title: Vendor Management Policy
summary: Policy for managing vendor relationships and SLAs
content: All strategic vendors must be registered in the Vendor Management System. Contracts over $100K require Legal review. Annual vendor performance reviews are required for all preferred vendors. SLAs must be documented in the contract. Vendor risk assessments are conducted prior to onboarding new vendors.

title: Meeting Room Booking System
summary: How to book meeting rooms
content: Book meeting rooms via the Outlook calendar or the Condeco portal. Search for an available room by size and location. Rooms can be booked up to 4 weeks in advance. Cancel bookings you no longer need to free up space for others. AV equipment requests must be submitted 24 hours in advance to Facilities.

title: Asset Management Policy
summary: How company assets are tracked and managed
content: All assets with a value over $500 are tagged with a barcode and recorded in the Asset Management System. Assets are assigned to individuals who are responsible for their care. Annual asset audits are conducted by the Finance team. Lost or stolen assets must be reported to IT and Facilities immediately.

title: Quality Management Process
summary: Company quality management approach
content: The company maintains ISO 9001:2015 certification. Internal audits are conducted quarterly. Non-conformances are tracked via the QMS system (qualio.company.com). Corrective actions must be closed within 30 days. All employees are required to participate in the annual quality awareness session in January.

title: Risk Management Framework
summary: Overview of the enterprise risk management framework
content: The ERM framework is based on ISO 31000. Risk owners register risks in the GRC system. Risks are rated on a 5×5 likelihood-impact matrix. The Risk Register is reviewed quarterly by the Risk Committee. Top risks are reported to the Board. The risk appetite statement is approved annually by the Board.

title: Onboarding FAQ for New Hires
summary: Frequently asked questions for new employees
content: Q: When do I get my first payslip? A: At the end of your first complete month. Q: How do I request leave? A: Via the HR portal. Q: What are the core hours? A: 10 AM – 4 PM. Q: Who do I contact for IT issues? A: The helpdesk at helpdesk@company.com. Q: Can I work from home? A: Up to 3 days per week with manager approval.

title: Parental Leave Policy
summary: Maternity, paternity, and adoption leave entitlements
content: Primary carers are entitled to 26 weeks of paid leave at 100% salary and up to 26 additional weeks of unpaid leave. Secondary carers receive 4 weeks of paid leave. Adoption leave follows the same policy as maternity leave. Employees must notify HR at least 8 weeks before the expected leave start date.

title: Anti-Harassment Policy
summary: Zero-tolerance policy on harassment and discrimination
content: The company has a zero-tolerance approach to harassment of any kind, including verbal, physical, and sexual harassment. Any incident must be reported to HR or via the anonymous ethics hotline. All complaints are investigated thoroughly and confidentially. Perpetrators face disciplinary action up to and including dismissal.

title: Probation Period Guidelines
summary: How the probationary period works for new employees
content: All new employees serve a 3-month probationary period. At 6 weeks, a mid-probation review is conducted. At the end of 3 months, the manager confirms employment or extends the probation by up to 3 more months. Termination during probation requires 1 week notice. HR is notified at each stage.

title: Whistleblower Protection Policy
summary: Protection for employees who report misconduct
content: Employees who report in good faith concerns about illegal activity, safety risks, or policy violations are protected from retaliation. Reports can be made anonymously via the ethics hotline or in writing to the Chief Compliance Officer. All reports are investigated. Retaliation is a disciplinary offence.

title: Helpdesk Escalation Paths
summary: When and how to escalate IT support issues
content: Level 1 support handles password resets, basic connectivity, and software installs. If unresolved in 30 minutes, escalate to Level 2 (infrastructure and advanced applications). If unresolved in 2 hours, escalate to Level 3 (vendors and architects). Always document escalation history in the ServiceNow ticket.

title: Mobile Device Management Policy
summary: Policy for company and personal mobile devices
content: Company-issued phones are enrolled in Microsoft Intune MDM. BYOD is permitted with Intune enrollment for email access only. MDM enables remote wipe of company data. Employees must not jailbreak or root enrolled devices. Company data must not be stored in personal cloud services.

title: Software Licensing Compliance
summary: Ensuring compliance with software license agreements
content: The IT Asset Management team maintains the software license register. Annual license audits are conducted. Using unlicensed software is a violation of company policy and may expose the company to legal risk. Report any suspected unlicensed software to the IT helpdesk. Employees who install unlicensed software face disciplinary action.

title: Remote Desktop Access Guide
summary: How to use remote desktop to access office systems
content: Connect to the VPN first. Open the Remote Desktop client and enter the hostname of your office computer (found in the IT portal). Use your company credentials to log in. File transfers are restricted to company-approved methods. Remote sessions are logged and audited. Do not leave remote sessions unattended.

title: Acceptable Use Policy
summary: Acceptable use of company IT resources
content: Company IT resources are for business use only. Limited personal use is permitted provided it does not interfere with work. Prohibited: accessing illegal content, downloading pirated software, using company email for personal business, and sharing credentials. All activity on company systems is monitored.

title: Kubernetes Cluster Management
summary: Managing the production Kubernetes cluster
content: The production cluster runs on EKS in us-east-1. Namespaces are environment-specific (prod, staging, dev). Resource quotas are enforced per namespace. All deployments must use Helm charts stored in the company artifact registry. Node upgrades are scheduled during the monthly maintenance window.

title: CI/CD Pipeline Overview
summary: Company CI/CD pipeline architecture and usage
content: The CI/CD pipeline uses GitHub Actions for code repos and Jenkins for legacy systems. Build, test, and deploy stages are mandatory. Security scanning (Snyk) is integrated at the build stage. Deployments to production require a manual approval gate. Pipeline configurations are stored in each repo's .github/workflows folder.

title: Infrastructure as Code Standards
summary: Standards for infrastructure-as-code using Terraform
content: All infrastructure must be provisioned via Terraform, not manually. State files are stored in S3 with DynamoDB locking. Modules are published to the internal Terraform registry. Code reviews are required for all IaC PRs. Terraform plan output must be reviewed before apply in production.

title: Monitoring and Alerting Setup
summary: How to configure monitoring and alerts for services
content: All production services must have uptime, error rate, and latency monitors in Datadog. Alert thresholds: Error rate > 1% (P2), Latency p99 > 2s (P3), Service down (P1). Alerts route to PagerDuty and the on-call engineer. Dashboard templates are available in the Datadog catalog.

title: Database Administration Guide
summary: Database management standards and procedures
content: Production databases run on RDS (PostgreSQL and MySQL). Schema changes require a migration script approved by the DBA team. Backups are automated (daily snapshots, retained 35 days). Query performance reviews are conducted monthly. All DBA access to production requires a separate ticket and is logged.

title: Introduction to Python for Analysts
summary: Python programming basics for data analysts
content: This training covers Python fundamentals: variables, data types, control flow, functions, and libraries (Pandas, NumPy). By the end, analysts can load and clean CSV files, perform aggregations, and create basic visualisations with Matplotlib. Prerequisites: basic Excel skills. Duration: 8 hours self-paced on the LMS.

title: Data Visualization with Power BI
summary: Creating dashboards and reports in Power BI
content: Power BI Desktop is available in the Software Center. Connect to company data sources (SQL, SharePoint, Excel). Build interactive reports with slicers, filters, and drill-through. Publish to Power BI Service (powerbi.company.com). Reports shared in workspaces. Row-level security must be applied to sensitive datasets.

title: Agile and Scrum Guide
summary: How to run Agile projects using Scrum
content: Scrum events: Sprint Planning (first Monday), Daily Stand-up (15 min daily), Sprint Review (last Thursday), Sprint Retrospective (last Friday). Roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team. Use Jira for backlog management. Definition of Done must be agreed by the team. Velocity is tracked over time.

title: Customer Service Training
summary: Best practices for customer-facing interactions
content: Key principles: Active listening, empathy, clarity, and follow-through. Use the HEARD model for complaints: Hear, Empathize, Apologize, Resolve, Diagnose. Escalate unresolved issues to the team leader. Always confirm resolution with the customer. Update the CRM with all interaction notes.

title: Compliance Training — AML
summary: Anti-money laundering awareness training
content: All employees must complete AML training annually. Key topics: customer due diligence, suspicious activity indicators, reporting obligations, and record-keeping requirements. The company's nominated Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) is the Finance Director. Suspicious transactions must be reported immediately.

title: Quarterly Financial Review Process
summary: Process for conducting quarterly financial reviews
content: Quarterly reviews are held within 15 business days of quarter end. Finance prepares a pack including P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, and variance analysis vs. budget. The CFO chairs the review with all department heads. Action items are tracked in the Finance Actions Register and reviewed monthly.

title: Capital Expenditure Policy
summary: Policy for capital expenditure approval
content: CapEx over $10K requires a business case approved by the CFO. The business case must include: cost-benefit analysis, ROI calculation, and payback period. CapEx assets are depreciated per the company depreciation policy (3 years for IT equipment, 5 years for office furniture, 10 years for building improvements). Annual CapEx budget is set in the budgeting process.

title: Treasury and Cash Management
summary: Company treasury and cash management policy
content: The treasury function manages cash positions, FX exposure, and short-term investments. Daily cash positions are reported by 9 AM. FX hedging is required for exposures over $500K. Surplus cash is invested in approved money market funds. The company maintains a minimum cash reserve of $2M.

title: Internal Transfer Pricing
summary: Guidelines for intercompany transfer pricing
content: All intercompany transactions must be priced at arm's length per the OECD guidelines. Transfer pricing documentation is maintained by the Tax team. Intercompany agreements must be in place before transactions commence. Annual TP reviews are conducted by the Tax Controller with external advisor support.

title: Revenue Recognition Policy
summary: How the company recognizes revenue
content: Revenue is recognized per IFRS 15 — when control of goods or services transfers to the customer. Contract reviews are required for all contracts over $1M. Variable consideration is estimated using the most likely amount method. Deferred revenue is recognized as the performance obligations are satisfied.

title: Capacity Management Process
summary: How to plan and manage resource capacity
content: Capacity reviews are held monthly. Resource demand is forecast 3 months ahead. Bottlenecks are escalated to the Operations Manager. Hiring requests must be raised at least 8 weeks before the required start date. Contractors can be engaged for up to 6 months with Director approval.

title: Key Performance Indicators Framework
summary: Defining and tracking KPIs across the business
content: Each department must define 5–10 KPIs aligned to strategic objectives. KPIs are tracked monthly and reported in the Operations Review. Use SMART criteria for KPI definition. KPI dashboards are built in Power BI. KPIs are reviewed annually in the strategy planning cycle.

title: Procurement Policy
summary: Company procurement policy and guidelines
content: All purchases must follow the procurement policy. Three quotes are required for purchases between $5K and $50K. A formal tender process is required for purchases over $50K. Sole-source procurement requires documented justification and Director approval. All suppliers must be on the approved vendor list.

title: Customer Complaint Handling
summary: Process for handling customer complaints
content: Log all complaints in the CRM within 1 hour of receipt. Acknowledge the customer within 2 hours. Resolve within 5 business days or escalate to the Customer Experience Manager. Root cause analysis is required for all complaints. Monthly complaint trend reports are reviewed by the Operations Director.

title: Supply Chain Management
summary: Managing the company supply chain
content: The supply chain team manages procurement, inventory, and logistics. Safety stock levels are reviewed quarterly. Lead times are tracked per supplier. Single-source dependencies are flagged as a supply chain risk. Dual sourcing is the preferred strategy for critical components.

title: Flexible Working Request Process
summary: How to submit a formal flexible working request
content: Employees with at least 26 weeks of service can request flexible working arrangements. Submit the request form to HR at least 3 months before the desired start date. Requests will be considered within 3 months. Valid business reasons are required to reject a request. Appeals can be raised with the HR Director.

title: Return to Work Process
summary: Process for returning to work after extended absence
content: An informal return-to-work meeting is required after any absence of 3 or more days. After extended absence (4+ weeks), a phased return plan may be agreed. Occupational health referrals are available. Medical certificates are required for absences over 7 days. HR maintains all records confidentially.

title: Network Access Control Policy
summary: Policy for controlling access to the corporate network
content: Network access is controlled via 802.1X authentication. Devices must be enrolled in Intune and compliant with endpoint policies. Guest Wi-Fi is isolated from the corporate network. Unauthorized devices detected on the network are automatically quarantined. NAC logs are reviewed weekly by the Security team.

title: Log Management and SIEM
summary: Centralized logging and SIEM configuration
content: All production systems must forward logs to the central SIEM (Splunk). Log retention is 12 months online and 7 years in cold storage. Security alerts are triaged by the SOC team 24/7. SIEM rules are reviewed quarterly. Anomaly detection uses ML-based baselines. Log tampering is a security incident.

title: Patch Management for Endpoints
summary: Managing software patches on employee devices
content: Endpoints are managed via Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager (MECM). Critical patches are deployed within 72 hours of release. All other patches are deployed within 14 days. Patch compliance dashboards are available in MECM. Devices with outstanding critical patches are flagged to the Security team.

title: Third-Party Risk Assessment
summary: Process for assessing third-party supplier risk
content: All new third-party suppliers must complete a risk questionnaire before onboarding. Risk is rated on financial, operational, cyber, and compliance dimensions. High-risk suppliers require additional due diligence and annual reviews. The Third-Party Risk Register is maintained by the Risk team.

title: Data Classification Policy
summary: How to classify and handle data by sensitivity
content: Data is classified as: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Classification labels are applied in Microsoft Purview. Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Sharing Confidential data externally requires manager approval. Training on data classification is mandatory for all employees.

title: Identity and Access Management
summary: Managing user identities and access rights
content: Access is provisioned based on role (RBAC). New access requests are submitted via ServiceNow. Access reviews are conducted quarterly; unused accounts are disabled after 90 days. Privileged access requires an approved PAM session (CyberArk). All access changes are logged and auditable.

title: Marketing Campaign Approval Process
summary: How to get marketing campaigns approved
content: All marketing campaigns must be approved by the Marketing Director and Legal before launch. Submit the campaign brief at least 4 weeks before the launch date. Legal review takes up to 5 business days. Final approvals must be signed off in the Campaign Management System. Post-campaign reports are required within 2 weeks.

title: Incident Post-Mortem Template
summary: Template and guidelines for incident post-mortems
content: Post-mortems are blameless and required for all P1 and P2 incidents. Complete within 5 business days of incident resolution. Sections: Incident timeline, root cause analysis, impact assessment, action items with owners and due dates. Share with affected stakeholders. Track action items in Jira.

title: Succession Planning Guide
summary: How to plan for key role succession
content: Succession plans are required for all Director-level and above positions. Identify at least 2 internal candidates per key role. Assess readiness: Ready Now, 1-2 years, 3+ years. Development plans are created for identified successors. Succession plans are reviewed annually in the Talent Review process.

title: ITIL v4 Foundation Reference
summary: Quick reference guide for ITIL v4 practices
content: Key ITIL v4 concepts: Service Value System (SVS), Service Value Chain, Four Dimensions Model, and 34 management practices. The Guiding Principles: Focus on value, Start where you are, Progress iteratively, Collaborate and promote visibility, Think and work holistically, Keep it simple and practical, Optimise and automate.

title: API Integration Standards
summary: Company standards for API design and integration
content: All internal APIs must follow REST conventions. Authentication via OAuth 2.0 / JWT. Rate limiting is enforced (1000 req/min per client). API documentation must be published to the internal API Portal (Swagger). Versioning: URI versioning (v1, v2). Breaking changes require a 6-month deprecation notice.

title: Security Incident Response Plan
summary: Plan for responding to security incidents
content: Security incidents are triaged by the SOC. The SIRT is activated for confirmed breaches. Phases: Preparation, Identification, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, Lessons Learned. The CISO notifies the CEO and Legal within 1 hour of a confirmed breach. Regulatory notifications follow relevant obligations (GDPR 72h).

title: Office Facilities Guide
summary: Everything you need to know about our office facilities
content: Office hours are 7 AM – 8 PM. Parking is available in basement levels 1 and 2. The cafeteria is open 7:30 AM – 3 PM. Gym access is available for all employees (register at reception). Quiet zones are on floors 4 and 5. Lockers are available from the Facilities desk. Recycling stations are on each floor.

title: Environmental Sustainability Policy
summary: Company commitment to environmental sustainability
content: The company targets net-zero emissions by 2040. Energy consumption is tracked monthly. Single-use plastics are banned in all offices. Business travel is offset through approved carbon credit schemes. The Sustainability team reports quarterly to the Board ESG Committee.

title: Remote Work Security Guide
summary: Security best practices for remote workers
content: Always use the VPN when connecting to company resources. Lock your screen when stepping away. Do not use public Wi-Fi without the VPN. Encrypt sensitive files before emailing. Enable full-disk encryption on your laptop (BitLocker). Report suspicious emails to security@company.com. Attend the quarterly remote security refresher.

title: Employee Self-Service Portal Guide
summary: How to use the employee self-service portal
content: The ESS portal (ess.company.com) allows you to: view payslips, submit leave requests, update personal details, access the employee handbook, enroll in training, and manage benefits. Log in with your company credentials. If you cannot access the portal, contact the HR helpdesk at hr@company.com.

title: Git Version Control Standards
summary: Company standards for Git usage and branching
content: Use the GitFlow branching strategy. Main branches: main (production), develop (integration). Feature branches: feature/[ticket-id]-description. Commit messages must follow Conventional Commits format. PRs require at least 1 approval and passing CI checks. Force pushes to main and develop are prohibited.

title: Container Security Standards
summary: Security standards for containerized workloads
content: All container images must be scanned by Snyk before deployment. Base images must be from the approved registry. Containers must run as non-root. Resource limits (CPU/memory) are mandatory. Secrets must be injected via Kubernetes Secrets or Vault — not environment variables. Images are re-scanned weekly.

title: Succession Planning — Technical Roles
summary: Succession planning guide for technical leadership
content: Technical succession planning identifies and develops high-potential engineers for senior roles. Create individual development plans covering: mentoring, stretch assignments, certifications, and cross-team exposure. Technical succession is reviewed annually at the Engineering Leadership Off-site.

title: Power Platform Governance
summary: Governance model for Microsoft Power Platform
content: The Power Platform CoE manages tenant-level governance. All production Power Apps must be reviewed by IT before go-live. Environment strategy: Dev, Test, Prod. Data connectors to sensitive systems require IT approval. A quarterly review identifies apps that are no longer used and reclaims premium licenses.

title: Accounts Receivable Process
summary: Managing accounts receivable and collections
content: Invoices are issued within 2 business days of service delivery. Payment terms are Net-30 unless contractually different. Overdue accounts (30+ days) receive an automated reminder. 60-day overdue accounts are escalated to the AR Manager. Legal action may be initiated at 90 days overdue after management approval.

title: Foreign Exchange Policy
summary: Policy for managing foreign exchange exposure
content: All FX exposures over $250K must be reported to Treasury. Hedging instruments approved: forward contracts and options. Speculative FX trading is strictly prohibited. Monthly FX exposure reports are reviewed by the CFO. The company's functional currency is USD.

title: Workplace Ergonomics Guide
summary: Setting up an ergonomic workspace
content: Adjust your chair so your feet are flat on the floor. The top of your monitor should be at eye level. Keep your keyboard and mouse close to avoid overreaching. Take a 5-minute break every hour. The Facilities team provides ergonomic assessments on request. Report any musculoskeletal discomfort to occupational health early.

title: ETL Pipeline Overview
summary: Introduction to the company ETL data pipeline
content: The ETL pipeline ingests knowledge article metadata from CSV exports, transforms and cleanses the data using Pandas, and loads it into the analytics database. Key stages: Extract (read CSV), Transform (deduplicate, normalise categories, parse tags), Load (upsert into the reporting tables). The pipeline is orchestrated via a CLI script and can be triggered from the admin dashboard.

title: Data Warehouse Architecture
summary: Company data warehouse architecture overview
content: The data warehouse is built on Amazon Redshift. Sources: operational databases, SaaS API feeds, and CSV/file ingestion pipelines. Data is modelled in a star schema. The staging layer cleans and deduplicates. The analytics layer serves Power BI and ad hoc queries. Refresh cadence: daily at 2 AM UTC.

title: Machine Learning Platform Guide
summary: Introduction to the company ML platform
content: The ML platform (SageMaker) supports model training, evaluation, and deployment. Data scientists must use the approved feature store for training data. Models are versioned in MLflow. Production models require a model card and bias assessment. Inference endpoints are monitored for data drift.

title: Zero Trust Security Model
summary: Overview of the zero trust security architecture
content: Zero trust assumes no implicit trust based on network location. All access requests are verified: user identity, device health, and least-privilege. Key controls: MFA everywhere, conditional access policies, microsegmentation, endpoint compliance checks, and continuous monitoring. The ZTA roadmap targets full implementation by 2027.

title: Company Strategy 2025–2030
summary: Overview of the company's 5-year strategic plan
content: The 2025–2030 strategy focuses on four pillars: Customer Centricity, Operational Excellence, Digital Transformation, and Sustainable Growth. Each pillar has OKRs defined at the Board level. Annual strategy reviews assess progress and adjust priorities. The strategy is communicated company-wide each January.
